title: Cache cohort rebalance storm — root cause analysis and mitigation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures the post-incident follow-up for a multi-tenant KV cache disruption on 2026-02-28 caused by an aggressive cohort rebalance. The rebalance interaction with prefetch and the slab eviction heuristics caused an amplified eviction storm, elevated memory churn, and degraded tail latency for multiple tenants. The goal of this ticket is to document the root cause, capture action items (short and medium term), and define a safe rollout plan for the fixes so we can prevent recurrence without regressing throughput or unit cost.
incident_summary: At ~2026-02-28 09:42 UTC a rolling control-plane job initiated a cohort rebalance across kvcache shards to reassign hot tenant segments. The rebalance moved high-KV-density segments into shards that already had warm KV-prefetch pipelines. The combination of simultaneous insert-heavy handoffs and aggressive prefetch budgets saturated the evictor, triggered cross-shard eviction cascades, and produced memory spikes followed by a period of elevated tail latency and 503 errors for affected routes. Automated fallback to a lower-capacity model reduced throughput but increased cost and recovery time.
root_cause:
Multiple interacting factors:
- A new cohort-rebalancer version (rolled in the same deploy window) removed a short random jitter between handoff operations, turning staggered moves into synchronized waves.
- Prefetch aggressiveness is configured at cohort granularity; when many hot cohorts landed on a single shard, prefetch budgets multiplied and forced the evictor into pathological churn.
- Eviction scoring uses a decay window biased toward recent access; sudden influx of new entries temporarily depressed scores for long-lived items, causing useful entries to be evicted (cache poisoning of hot sets).
- Observability lacked a compact signal for ‘rebalance intensity’ and the prefetch *multiplier* per-shard, so the control plane could not detect buildup early enough to abort the rebalance wave.
timeline: 2026-02-28 09:35 UTC: Control-plane rebalance job scheduled as part of capacity smoothing.
2026-02-28 09:42 UTC: Rebalance executed without jitter; ~120 cohort moves initiated within 45s.
2026-02-28 09:44 UTC: Grafana alert: kvcache_shard_memory_used > 85% on three shards (dashboard link in attachments).
2026-02-28 09:46 UTC: First 503s observed on latency-sensitive routes; ops paged.
2026-02-28 09:55 UTC: Temporary throttle and slow-failover to lower-capacity model enacted; downstream error rates stabilized but throughput dropped 22%.
2026-02-28 12:10 UTC: Hotfix: rebalancer reverted to previous version with jitter; memory usage returned to baseline over 40 minutes.
2026-02-28 13:00 UTC: Incident declared resolved; follow-up investigation opened (this ticket).
action_items: A1: Implement ephemeral jitter and maximum concurrent-moves throttle in the cohort rebalancer (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 5).
A2: Add per-shard 'prefetch multiplier' metric and an alert when multiplier * active_cohorts > threshold (owner: Mei Chen, estimate: 3).
A3: Introduce a pre-rebalance dry-run that computes projected eviction pressure using current shard state; abort or rate-limit if projected pressure > 0.75 (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 8).
A4: Update eviction scoring to include an 'incoming-move' penalty that protects resident keys during handoff windows (owner: Kevin Lopez, estimate: 8).
A5: Create a shadow-rebalance mode to exercise new rebalancer logic in prod without applying moves (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 5).
A6: Dashboard and runbook updates: add a 'rebalance intensity' panel, playbook steps for quiescing rebalances under memory pressure, and Slack incident shortcuts (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2).
A7: Run a targeted chaos test in staging simulating 100 concurrent cohort moves with prefetched workloads and validate evictor stability (owner: Test Infra, estimate: 3).
decisions: Decide to delay enabling concurrent rebalance optimizations in runtime-1.20 until shadow-rebalance testing completes.
Prefer soft-guards (jitter, throttle, dry-run, monitoring) over hard capacity reductions to avoid unnecessary cost regressions.
Eviction scoring changes will be behind a feature flag with per-cluster defaults to allow phased rollout.
followups: Confirm telemetry for new metrics is present in all regions and add synthetic alerts to CI (by 2026-03-15).
Schedule a cross-team review (SRE, runtime, infra, product) after shadow-rebalance runbook sign-off (by 2026-03-18).
Audit previous rebalancer deploys to ensure no other production changes removed jittering elsewhere (by 2026-03-12).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Shadow-rebalance can be executed in prod for 24h with no applied moves and no sustained increase (>5%) in evictor churn metrics.
AC2: Per-shard 'prefetch multiplier' metric is available and alerts trigger in staging during induced load tests.
AC3: Rebalancer with jitter+throttle can move 500 cohorts per hour without causing shard memory > 80% in the worst-case tested workload.
AC4: Eviction scoring change behind feature flag shows <1% RPS regression in perfbench and reduces eviction of long-lived keys under simulated handoffs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: implement telemetry and dry-run simulation (runtime-1.20 alpha). Phase 1: deploy shadow-rebalance behind a flag and run 72h in prod with synthetic traffic and on-call observation. Phase 2: enable jitter+throttle by default and keep eviction-scoring change off. Phase 3: enable eviction-scoring change in a limited canary group with automatic rollback if evictor_churn_rate > baseline + 10%. Monitor for 7 days after each phase.
notes: SRE feedback: prefer automated abort over manual interventions for waves where projected pressure > threshold; agreed to add a ‘circuit-breaker’ flag (Slack review 2026-03-02).
Design review: moving eviction-protection into scoring increases code complexity and must be accompanied by unit/bench coverage (Design review notes: doc link in attachments).
PM comment: customer-facing SLO impact was short but visible; customers were notified via status page and follow-up emails. Keep comms template for similar incidents.
